questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was an English-speaking country, it was far away and a place I haven't been.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got very many mails with information, and team-meetings. But almost to much, it would have been nice if it could be more simple, and only the important information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not any the first days from the university. I met at the university with some students from my home university, but nobody knew why we were there when we told them that we were exchange students. It was nice when the exchange events started, after the into-week. At the exchange events both the students and the assistance were very open and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Do it as early as possible. We didn't. Live close to campus, because the transportation is not so good.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to have roommates that also are exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There wasn't any housing available at campus, and we got told that very late after application.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine, follow the links

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could send an email to get help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes you can change your classes after you started, but it's much easier if dont need to. If you're not sure, maybe take one more and drop the one you like the least after the 2 weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three level 3 courses and one levet 2 course. I think the level was fine, but a bit heavy workload of some of them when you're on exchange.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, much more by hand. Not used to remember that much, mostly how to use it and understand it. It was much more about memorizing. Its also very different that you have midterms, and they counts too. So you have more control on how you're doing, doing the semester, which make the exam in the end very chill, compared to when the exams count 100% of the grade. It's almost impossible to fail.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 3HH3 International Trade
ECON 2B03 Analysis of Economic Data
ECON 3E03 Applied Econometrics
ECON 3BE3 Behavioural Economics

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked ECON 3BE3 Behavioural Economics, it was new to me and very interesting. Learned a lot, but no homework and only one assignment.

questions.answer: That transportation in that city was free for exchange students

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Milk and cheese was more expensive. Cafe coffee a bit cheaper. But confusing that they dont include taxes in the price, and the taxes was different for each thing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Very very many. Almost everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did pilates Classes and the gym. I did pilates with another exchange student. I think it was a nice way to see each other.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the other big citys around. And join the exchange activity.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone say "Thank you" when they leave the bus, I think that was cute

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find out why you are doing exchange, and choose things that supports that. Because there will be SO many thinks to do.
2. Reach out, and the first 3 weeks is very important to socialize 
3. The best coffee on campus is the Grind Cafe

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think it was very nice to start an everyday in a new place. I got more comfortable speaking English. The last weeks I wanted to get the last joy out of the experience, studying together, partying and so, it felled so fulfilling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The transportation to school took one hour, even though it was only 9 km away...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
